newsitem.title: USA: Celgene files for leprosy indication.
newsitem.headline: Celgene files for leprosy indication.

text.p: Celgene Corp said on Wednesday that it has filed its New Drug Application for the use of SYNOVIR (thalidomide) to treat erythema nodosum leprosum, a leprosy related condition.
The agency has 60 days to review a submitted new drug application for completeness and applicability, the company said.
Once an NDA is accepted as filed, the FDA undertakes the process of evaluating the drug on its merits of safety and efficacy, the company said.
Erythema nodosum leprosum is a painful inflammatory condition occurring in 30-50 percent of patients with leprosy and produces lesions, fever, and wasting, the company said.
Thalidomide has been used in the treatment of the ailment worldwide for over 25 years and has been recommended as the treatment of choice by the World Health Organization, the company said.
